newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges PLO to fire officials inciting killings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges PLO to fire officials inciting killings.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said Wednesday that Palestinian officials who called for the kiling of Arabs who sold land to Jews should be "repudiated or fired".

But spokesman Nicholas Burns rebuffed calls by House of Representatives speaker Newt Gingrich for the possible suspension of aid to the Palestinians because of recent murders of Arabs suspected of making such sales.

Three Arab land dealers have been killed since the Palestinian Authority last month revived a Jordanian law banning land sales to Jews, an offence punishable by death. Jordan ruled the West Bank until 1967.

Gingrich said Tuesday that those responsible were acting like Nazis and threatened to block aid to the Palestinian Authority unless its leaders denounced the killings, whose perpetrators have not been identified.
Burns said senior Palestinian justice officials, whom he did not identify, "have publicly called for political assassinations. And that's wrong and those people ought to be repudiated or fired."

Speaking at a regular news briefing, he declined to say if he was referring to Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen, who was quoted May 4 as saying that Palestinians who sold land to Jews faced execution.

Burns said Gingrich was right to call attention to the problem but the administration differed from the speaker "in one respect, and that is, we think that American aid should continue to the Palestinians".

"American aid is directed towards the Palestinian people. It does not go to the Palestinian Authority," he said. Washington has pledged $500 million to the Palestinians over five years, of which $220 million has been handed over.

Gingrich's comments were welcomed by Israel but were called "disgusting" by Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat, who said Gingrich was "fully aware that the Palestinian Authority will not allow people to take the law into their own hands".
Burns said the United States welcomed what he said were assurances by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat that he would hold responsible officials who had called for the killing of land dealers.
